title: upgrade leaves an undeclared closed thread's stale views for the operator to delete by hand
body:
**`upgrade` on a dormant estate leaves an undeclared closed thread's stale views for the operator to delete by hand.** Measured by courses-vc on the nested Courses estate, last touched at 3.0.0, 2026-09-13: `intent upgrade` wrote `.intentfiles` declaring the one WIP thread, so the two closed threads became undeclared; `sync --to-disk` then skipped them, as the manifest says it should; and `organize` refused to dehydrate their eleven views because each still carried the 3.0.0 footer, which doctor classes as `stale-render`, footer-only. The remedy text was right and worked (delete the views, re-run), but it put an eleven-file deletion in the operator's hands on an estate the tool had just told them was upgraded.

**The gap is between two correct rules.** The manifest rule says an undeclared thread's views are not rendered; the organize rule says a view it cannot re-render byte-identically is not its to remove. Between them a view rendered by an earlier binary for a thread that is now undeclared has no owner: nothing re-renders it and nothing removes it. `upgrade` is the one verb that knows it just changed the declaration, and the one place that gap can be closed without a new rule.

**Ruled under the pen, 2026-09-13:** `upgrade`, after writing `.intentfiles`, dehydrates the views of every thread it left undeclared through the same path `organize --apply` uses, reporting each path, so an upgraded estate reads clean on `doctor -v` and `organize -v` without a hand deletion. One test, one arm: a fixture with a closed thread's 3.0.0-footer views and no manifest, upgraded, has those views gone and the thread's canon untouched. After the thread.
